Subject: Intermittent timeouts & 502s from Cerberus-3b (production)

Hi Priyom,

We're seeing a burst of timeouts and 502/504 responses from model cerberus-3b on our production service starting around 08:50 PDT. The failures show up on longer generation requests (>= 1k tokens) — streaming connections are dropped mid-response and retrying hits the same errors. This is affecting ~15% of our production requests and causing degraded UX for a small percentage of critical workflows.

I attached a short server-side timeline from our side (we can share logs if helpful). Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing any model-level anomalies or recent infra changes? We have a demo scheduled tomorrow so this is pretty high priority for us.

Thanks,
Sam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@velvetanalytics.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: [Incident INF-4821] Triage update — Cerberus-3b elevated errors

Status update (11:05 PDT):

- What we see: Cerberus-3b showed a sharp increase in tail latencies and 502/504 responses for streaming/generation requests with context lengths >1024 tokens. Error rate peaked at ~18% for affected hosts between 08:45–09:40 PDT and decayed after mitigations.

- Immediate mitigations applied (11:00 PDT):
  * Rolled request routing away from the subset of hosts running the recently deployed quantized kernel (vQ1.2) to the stable kernel pool.
  * Increased autoscaling target for cerberus-3b GPU pool for US region (added 6 reserved workers, bumped burst capacity).
  * Enabled aggressive KV cache trimming for long-session workloads to reduce memory fragmentation.

- What reduced the error rate: routing away from vQ1.2 hosts and the reserve worker addition visibly reduced 502/504 occurrences by ~70% in the first 10 minutes after action. Stream disconnects decreased but we observed some residual latency for long sequences until KV cache reclamation finished.

- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a kernel-level regression in vQ1.2 that surfaces under long-sequence KV-cache patterns after a recent micro-optimization. The regression causes intermittent kernel panics (handled by the runtime with 5xx responses) and exacerbates memory fragmentation leading to timeouts on long runs.

Attachments: cerberus-3b-metrics-snapshot.png (showing host-level error rates and heap fragmentation timeline).

Next steps:
  1) Rollback vQ1.2 from the affected US host pool (in progress). ETA 60–90m.
  2) QA a patch to the quantized kernel that removes the micro-optimization path causing fragmentation; test on staging.
  3) Post-incident RCA and a follow-up note with impact metrics and mitigations (will share draft by EOD).

We will keep this bridge open until the rollback and stabilization complete. Marcus is coordinating the kernel rollback; I'll coordinate communication with Velvet.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Incident: Cerberus-3b — recovery confirmation & post-incident plan

Sam — final update and next steps (post-bridge):

Summary of impact:
- Time window: 2027-07-07 08:45–09:40 PDT.
- Client impact: Approximately 15–18% error rate on long-generation requests for Velvet Analytics during the window; most requests recovered with retries after 09:10 once routing and scaling were in place.

What caused it:
- Root cause: a regression in the newly deployed quantized kernel (vQ1.2) that caused intermittent kernel failures and accelerated KV cache fragmentation on long-context workloads (>=1k tokens). The combination led to 5xx responses and streaming disconnects for a subset of hosts.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: Routed traffic away from vQ1.2 hosts, added reserve workers, and enabled KV cache trimming (completed within 11:00 PDT).
- Rollback: vQ1.2 rolled back from the affected US pool at 11:25 PDT on 2027-07-07. Host stability confirmed by 11:40 PDT.
- Remediation: Patch to kernel submitted to staging for validation (INF-4821). We will only reintroduce the quantized kernel after multi-variant testing for long-context loads and explicit canarying with throttled traffic.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommend:
- If you have repeated long-stream workloads, consider setting a request-level max_length or incremental checkpoints in the short term while we complete a hardened re-roll of vQ1.2.

Follow-ups we will deliver in 72 hours:
1) Full RCA document (link below) with host-level timelines and error counts.
2) A patch schedule and testing plan for reintroducing the quantized kernel.
3) A compensating config option allowing customers to opt-out of quantized kernel routes for critical endpoints.

We've attached the draft RCA and the metrics snapshot from the bridge for your review. Please let me know if you want a short walk-through call — happy to jump on one.

Thanks for your patience, and again apologies for the disruption. We're adding tighter pre-roll checks for any quantized kernel changes to prevent recurrence.

Best,
